newsitem.title: UK: Wet N. Sea crudes see little upside, buying slow.
newsitem.headline: Wet N. Sea crudes see little upside, buying slow.

text.p: As North Sea traders and refiners waited further news on the price and possible outlets for April Brent, buyers of other grades held back and few deals were reported.

"Everyone is so nervous and they (the buyers) all have an eye on the Brent to see what will happen there. People selling other grades don't know how to pitch them till they see what happens to all the Brents out already," one North Sea equity holder said.
"Even if some crude moves out of the area (Northwest Europe) this market still looks bad fundamentally," he added.
Following the trade of a Mar 31-April 2 Brent cargo at May Brent -90 cents on Tuesday, the market took a further downturn. CFDs lost ground as did the prompt April/May.
The April/May traded at a low -30 cents after talk early in the day around -20 cents.
Talk on next week's Mar 31-April 4 CFDs was around May -56, just up from the low of the day of May -60 cents.
Other wet deals heard, though not confirmed, were a Forties on April 10-12 dates at around dated Brent -5 cents. One equity holder saw the market at dated Brent -10/-5 cents.
A second decade Ekofisk was heard to have traded around dated Brent +2-4 cents but some saw the market around evens with Brent.
